sonnet.problem: The choice card follows only the opening card, which covers verse 1. Nothing sets up verse 2, so the baker cannot reason out 'incense' and has to guess a detail (incense, showbread or firstfruits) by luck. This is the same kind of detail-guessing the docs mark as a bad example for poetry.
sonnet.rule: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

sonnet.problem: The card asks the baker to name the everyday picture David uses (plowing the soil, scattering chaff or a smashed jar). The only card before it, card 4, tells verse 7 with the picture trimmed off. Nothing lets the baker reason to 'plowing', and 'wind scattering the chaff' fits 'scattered' at least as well, so the pick comes down to luck.
sonnet.rule: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.
